creatingProposals.step2: Enter the event description — be as specific as possible about the venue and requirements
creatingProposals.step3: CueQuote's AI generates a complete equipment list with quantities and pricing
creatingProposals.step4: Review and edit: add, remove, or adjust any line items
creatingProposals.step5: Download as a branded PDF or share via a unique link
creatingProposals.tip: Use the share link feature to let clients view proposals online — they can approve directly from the link.

equipmentCatalog.title: Equipment Catalog
equipmentCatalog.content1: Your equipment catalog is the backbone of accurate proposals. CueQuote lets you maintain a detailed inventory of your gear with default pricing.
equipmentCatalog.content2: Equipment is organized into categories: Audio, Lighting, Video, Staging, Rigging, Power & Distribution, and Custom. Each item can have a name, description, default rental price, and internal notes.
equipmentCatalog.step2: Add items manually or import from a CSV spreadsheet
equipmentCatalog.step3: Set default rental prices per item — these will be used when AI generates proposals
equipmentCatalog.step4: Organize items into categories for easy browsing
equipmentCatalog.tip: When you import from CSV, use columns: Name, Category, Price, Description. CueQuote will map them automatically.

clients.title: Clients
clients.content1: Keep all your client information organized in one place. CueQuote supports different client types to help you categorize your business relationships.
clients.content2: Each client record stores contact details, company information, and is linked to all their proposals — giving you a complete history of your quoting relationship.
clients.step1: Navigate to Clients and click "Add Client"
clients.step2: Fill in contact and company details
clients.step3: Select the client type: Direct, Agency, Venue, or Corporate
clients.step4: Link the client to new proposals from the proposal creation screen
clients.tip: Client types help you track where your business comes from. Use the "Agency" type for production companies that subcontract your services.

pdfTemplates.title: PDF Templates
pdfTemplates.content1: CueQuote offers four professionally designed PDF templates so your proposals always look polished and on-brand.
pdfTemplates.content2: Each template automatically applies your company logo, brand color, and contact information. You can switch templates at any time — existing proposals will update to use the new template when re-downloaded.
pdfTemplates.step1: Modern — Clean lines, generous white space, contemporary feel. Best for tech-forward clients.
pdfTemplates.step2: Bold — Strong typography, high-contrast layout. Great for making a statement.
pdfTemplates.step3: Classic — Traditional proposal format with structured sections. Ideal for corporate clients.
pdfTemplates.step4: Minimal — Stripped-back design focused on content. Perfect when simplicity matters.
pdfTemplates.tip: You can set a default template in Settings, but override it per proposal if needed. Your brand color is applied to headings, accents, and borders.

termsDetails.title: Terms & Details
termsDetails.content1: Every proposal can include customizable terms and conditions, payment terms, and inclusion/exclusion lists. These sections build trust and set clear expectations with your clients.
termsDetails.content2: You can set defaults that apply to all new proposals, then customize per proposal as needed.
termsDetails.step1: Go to Settings → Proposal Defaults to set your standard terms
termsDetails.step2: Edit inclusions: what's covered in the quoted price (e.g., delivery, setup, operator)
termsDetails.step3: Edit exclusions: what's not included (e.g., power supply, venue access fees)
termsDetails.step4: Set payment terms: deposit percentage, payment schedule, accepted methods
termsDetails.step5: Add your full Terms & Conditions — these appear on the last page of the PDF
termsDetails.tip: Each proposal has its own copy of these terms. Changing the defaults won't affect existing proposals — only new ones.

billingPlans.title: Billing & Plans
billingPlans.content1: CueQuote offers flexible plans to match your business size. Start free and upgrade as you grow.
billingPlans.step1: Free — 3 proposals/month, 1 user, basic PDF template
billingPlans.step2: Starter (€29/mo) — 10 proposals/month, 1 user, full branding, client management
billingPlans.step3: Pro (€79/mo) — 40 proposals/month, 5 users, custom templates, priority support
billingPlans.step4: Business (€179/mo) — 120 proposals/month, 20 users, API access, dedicated support
billingPlans.tip: You can upgrade or downgrade at any time from Settings → Billing. Changes take effect at the start of the next billing cycle.

settings.title: Settings
settings.content1: The Settings page is where you configure everything about your CueQuote workspace. Keeping your settings up-to-date ensures every proposal reflects your brand accurately.
settings.step1: Company Profile — Business name, address, phone, email, and website
settings.step2: Logo — Upload your company logo (PNG or SVG recommended, max 2MB)
settings.step3: Brand Color — Choose a hex color that matches your brand; applied to all PDF templates
settings.step4: Currency — Set your default currency (USD, EUR, GBP, PLN, and more)
settings.step5: Language — Set the proposal language (affects PDF headings and labels)
settings.step6: Proposal Defaults — Default template, terms, inclusions, exclusions, and payment terms
settings.tip: Your logo looks best at a minimum of 400px wide. CueQuote will automatically resize it for the PDF.

invoicing.title: Invoicing
invoicing.content1: CueQuote lets you create professional invoices directly from your proposals. Once a proposal is sent or accepted, you can generate a deposit or full invoice with one click — complete with your company branding and payment instructions.
invoicing.content2: Before creating invoices, add your payment methods in Settings. You can configure bank transfer details (IBAN, SWIFT), PayPal, or Wise. These details appear on every invoice PDF you generate, so clients know exactly how to pay.
invoicing.step1: Go to Settings and add your payment methods (bank account, PayPal, or Wise) under Payment Information
invoicing.step2: Open a sent or accepted proposal and click "Create Invoice" — choose between a deposit invoice or a full invoice
invoicing.step3: Review the invoice editor: verify the invoice number, issue date, due date, line items, and totals
invoicing.step4: Select which payment method to display on the invoice from the dropdown
invoicing.step5: Download the invoice PDF — it includes your branding, line items, VAT, payment instructions, and reference number
invoicing.step6: Send the invoice to your client via email and track its status: Draft, Sent, Viewed, or Paid
invoicing.tip: Add at least one bank account in Settings — most B2B clients prefer bank transfer for AV equipment payments. Include the invoice number as the payment reference for easy reconciliation.

paymentTracking.title: Payment Tracking
paymentTracking.content1: CueQuote lets you record full and partial payments on invoices and track the complete payment history. When you record a payment, the invoice status updates automatically — partial when partially paid, paid when fully covered.
paymentTracking.content2: Every payment is logged with the amount, date, method, and optional reference number. You can view, delete, or add payments at any time. If you accidentally mark an invoice as paid, you can revert it with one click.
paymentTracking.step1: Open an invoice and click the green "Record Payment" button in the Summary sidebar
paymentTracking.step2: Enter the amount received, date, payment method (bank transfer, cash, card, check), and optional reference number
paymentTracking.step3: View all payments in the Payment History section below the invoice notes — each shows amount, date, method, and reference
paymentTracking.step4: To revert a paid invoice, click "Undo — mark as unpaid" below the Paid badge — it recalculates based on actual recorded payments
paymentTracking.step5: Change invoice status manually by clicking the status badge in the header — select from Draft, Sent, Viewed, Partial, Paid, Overdue, or Cancelled
paymentTracking.tip: Use the status dropdown to manually mark overdue invoices. The Record Payment button in the sidebar is the quickest way to log received funds.

correctiveInvoices.title: Corrective Invoices
correctiveInvoices.content1: When a sent or paid invoice needs corrections, CueQuote lets you issue a corrective invoice that references the original. The original stays untouched for audit purposes, and the correction shows exactly what changed with before/after values.
correctiveInvoices.content2: Corrective invoices follow professional invoicing standards used across the EU and are compatible with Poland's KSeF e-invoicing system. Each correction is linked to its original invoice with full traceability.
correctiveInvoices.step1: Open a sent, viewed, or paid invoice and click the correction icon (circular arrow) in the header toolbar
correctiveInvoices.step2: The system creates a new invoice with "/COR" suffix, pre-filled with all original line items and their values stored as snapshots
correctiveInvoices.step3: Edit the items that need correcting — modified items show the original total struck through next to the new total
correctiveInvoices.step4: Fill in the "Reason for Correction" field and send the corrective invoice to your client
correctiveInvoices.tip: The original invoice shows an amber banner linking to the correction, and the corrective invoice shows a blue banner linking back to the original — creating a complete audit trail.

smartSuggestions.title: Smart Suggestions
smartSuggestions.content1: CueQuote's Smart Suggestions engine analyzes your company's past proposals to provide intelligent recommendations. It detects items you frequently include but may have missed, flags pricing inconsistencies, and identifies items you use often but haven't added to your catalog.
smartSuggestions.content2: Smart Suggestions learns from your own data — the more proposals you create, the smarter it gets. It requires at least 3 sent proposals to generate meaningful recommendations. You can toggle it on or off at any time.
smartSuggestions.step1: Click the "Smart" lightbulb toggle in the proposal tab bar to enable suggestions — your preference is saved across sessions
smartSuggestions.step2: The "Missing Items" tab shows items you usually include but haven't added to this proposal, with confidence scores and one-click "Add" buttons
smartSuggestions.step3: The "Repricing" tab flags items priced more than 15% above or below your historical average, showing current vs average price with min-max range
smartSuggestions.step4: The "Add to Catalog" tab lists items used in 2+ proposals but missing from your equipment catalog — click to create catalog entries with average pricing
smartSuggestions.tip: Smart Suggestions is especially useful for preventing forgotten items and maintaining consistent pricing across proposals. The repricing tab catches accidental price changes when reusing items.

sharingTracking.title: Sharing & Tracking Proposals
sharingTracking.content1: CueQuote lets you share proposals with clients via unique links — no PDFs to email back and forth. When a client opens the link, you see exactly when they viewed it, how many times, and whether they accepted or declined.
sharingTracking.content2: Every proposal gets a shareable link that shows a professional, branded view of your proposal. Clients can review equipment, pricing, and terms, then accept or decline with one click. You get notified instantly when they respond.
sharingTracking.step1: Open any proposal and click the "Share" button in the header
sharingTracking.step2: Copy the unique share link and send it to your client via email, WhatsApp, or any messaging tool
sharingTracking.step3: Track views in real-time — see when the client opens the proposal and how many times they viewed it
sharingTracking.step4: When the client clicks "Accept" or "Decline" on the shared page, you receive an instant notification on your dashboard
sharingTracking.step5: Follow up strategically — if a client viewed but hasn't responded within 48 hours, it's time to reach out
sharingTracking.tip: Use the "Send Proposal" button to email the share link directly from CueQuote with a personal message. The email includes a summary of the proposal with a branded CTA button.

teamManagement.title: Team Management
teamManagement.content1: CueQuote supports multi-user teams with role-based access. The company owner can invite team members and assign roles that control what each person can see and do.
teamManagement.content2: There are four roles: Owner (full access, can manage billing and team), Admin (full access except billing), Sales (can create and manage proposals, clients, and catalog), and Viewer (read-only access to proposals and dashboard).
teamManagement.step1: Go to Team from the sidebar — you'll see all current team members with their roles
teamManagement.step2: Click "Invite Member" and enter their email address and select a role
teamManagement.step3: The invited person receives an email with a link to join your CueQuote workspace
teamManagement.step4: Once they accept, they appear on your team page and can access the dashboard based on their assigned role
teamManagement.step5: You can change roles or remove team members at any time from the Team page
teamManagement.tip: Use the Sales role for your quoting team — they can create proposals and manage clients but can't change billing or company settings.

scopeTemplates.title: Scope Templates
scopeTemplates.content1: Scope templates let you save and reuse proposal configurations for recurring event types. Instead of describing the same conference setup from scratch every time, save it as a template with pre-configured line items, quantities, and pricing.
scopeTemplates.content2: Templates come in two types: scope-only templates (just the event description and settings, AI still generates the equipment list) and full templates (complete with pre-configured line items that skip AI generation entirely).
scopeTemplates.step1: Go to Templates from the sidebar to view and manage your saved templates
scopeTemplates.step2: To create a template from scratch, click "New Template" and configure the event type, description, attendee range, and optionally add line items
scopeTemplates.step3: To save an existing proposal as a template, open the proposal editor and click "Save as Template" — all line items are captured
scopeTemplates.step4: When creating a new proposal, your templates appear as quick-start cards — click one to pre-fill the event description and settings
scopeTemplates.step5: Full templates (with line items) let you skip AI generation entirely — click "Use Template" to create an instant proposal
scopeTemplates.tip: Create templates for your most common event types: conference, gala dinner, product launch, hybrid event. Each template speeds up quoting by 80% for repeat event formats.

accountProfile.title: Account & Profile
accountProfile.content1: Your account page lets you manage your personal profile and security settings. This is separate from company settings — account settings are per-user, not shared with your team.
accountProfile.content2: You can update your display name (shown in the sidebar and on team pages), change your password, and view your account email. Your profile photo can be updated from the account page as well.
accountProfile.step1: Click your name at the bottom of the sidebar to open the Account page
accountProfile.step2: Edit your full name — this is displayed to your team members and in activity logs
accountProfile.step3: Change your password — enter your current password, then your new password (minimum 8 characters)
accountProfile.step4: Your email address is shown for reference but cannot be changed directly — contact support if you need to update it
accountProfile.tip: Use a professional full name — it appears on proposals and invoices when you're the assigned creator.

proposalLanguage.title: Per-Proposal Language
proposalLanguage.content1: CueQuote supports creating proposals in 5 languages: English, Polish, Arabic, German, and French. Each proposal can be generated in a different language — independent of your dashboard language.
proposalLanguage.content2: This is designed for AV companies working with international clients. An Arabic-speaking user can create an English proposal for an English-speaking client, and vice versa. The AI generates all content (item names, descriptions, inclusions, exclusions) in the chosen language, while keeping brand names and equipment model numbers untranslated.
proposalLanguage.step1: When creating a new proposal, select the language from the dropdown next to the Currency selector
proposalLanguage.step2: The language defaults to your dashboard language but can be changed per proposal
proposalLanguage.step3: Click Generate — the AI outputs all proposal text in the selected language
proposalLanguage.step4: The PDF also renders labels (Subtotal, Total, Terms, Payment Schedule, etc.) in the proposal's language
proposalLanguage.step5: You can always edit the generated text in the proposal editor after generation
proposalLanguage.tip: Catalog item brand names (Sennheiser, Shure, etc.) are kept untranslated regardless of the proposal language. The AI translates descriptive text while preserving product identifiers.

aiQuota.title: AI Generation Quota
aiQuota.content1: Each CueQuote plan includes a monthly AI proposal generation quota. Every time you generate a proposal using AI (including retries), it counts against your monthly limit.
aiQuota.content2: Before generating, CueQuote shows a confirmation dialog telling you how many generations you have remaining this month. This helps you avoid wasting a slot on an incomplete description. The dialog is skipped for admin and enterprise users.
aiQuota.step1: Free plan: 3 AI generations per month
aiQuota.step2: Starter plan: 10 AI generations per month
aiQuota.step3: Pro plan: 40 AI generations per month
aiQuota.step4: Business plan: 120 AI generations per month
aiQuota.step5: Manual edits to generated proposals are always free — only new AI generations count
aiQuota.tip: Write a detailed event description before clicking Generate. The more specific you are, the better the AI output — and the less likely you'll need to regenerate.

gettingStartedChecklist.title: Getting Started Checklist
gettingStartedChecklist.content1: When you first log in after signing up, the dashboard shows a Getting Started checklist at the top. This guides you through the essential setup steps to get your first proposal out the door.
gettingStartedChecklist.content2: Each step auto-completes as you perform the action — no manual checkboxes needed. Once all steps are done, the checklist shows a celebration message and can be dismissed permanently.
gettingStartedChecklist.step1: Create your account — automatically completed after signup
gettingStartedChecklist.step2: Set up your company — completed during onboarding (company name, address, brand color)
gettingStartedChecklist.step3: Upload your logo — go to Settings and upload your company logo (appears on every PDF)
gettingStartedChecklist.step4: Add equipment to your catalog — import your gear and prices for accurate AI proposals
gettingStartedChecklist.step5: Create your first proposal — describe an event and generate your first AI-powered quote
gettingStartedChecklist.tip: You can dismiss the checklist at any time by clicking the X button. It won't come back once dismissed.

regenerateProposals.title: Regenerate Proposals
regenerateProposals.content1: Instead of creating a new proposal from scratch, you can regenerate an existing one. This updates the line items while preserving your client, dates, venue, terms, and all other settings. Regenerating does not count against your monthly proposal quota.
regenerateProposals.content2: There are three regeneration modes: Full (replaces all line items with a fresh AI generation), Smart (keeps items you manually edited, replaces AI-generated ones), and From File (upload an updated specification document and regenerate based on it).

step1.title: Open the regenerate modal
step1.text: From the proposal editor, click the More menu (⋯) and select Regenerate Proposal. You can also click Regenerate from the proposals list page dropdown.

step2.title: Choose a mode
step2.text: Select Full to start fresh, Smart to keep your manual edits, or From File to upload an updated spec document. The From File option lets you attach PDF, Word, Excel, or image files.

step3.title: Select what to regenerate
step3.text: Choose whether to also regenerate the scope summary and inclusions/exclusions, or keep your existing ones. Only line items are regenerated by default.

step4.title: Review and adjust
step4.text: After regeneration, review the new line items in the Equipment tab. You can edit quantities, prices, and descriptions as usual. The proposal status remains unchanged.

regenerateProposals.tip: Regenerating is free — it does not use a proposal credit. Use it to quickly update proposals when requirements change.

riskAssessment.title: Risk Assessment Plan
riskAssessment.content1: CueQuote can generate an AI-powered risk assessment for your events. The risk plan identifies potential problems and provides specific mitigation strategies based on your event's equipment, venue, attendee count, and duration.
riskAssessment.content2: Risk assessment is available from the Risk Plan tab in the proposal editor. Starter plans get 3 basic categories (equipment, power, crew) in view-only mode. Pro plans unlock all 8 categories with full editing and PDF inclusion. Business plans add custom risk creation and regeneration.

step1.title: Open the Risk Plan tab
step1.text: In the proposal editor, click the Risk Plan tab next to Equipment and Terms & Details. If you're on a Free plan, you'll see an upgrade prompt.

step2.title: Generate the risk plan
step2.text: Click Generate Risk Plan. The AI analyzes your event details, equipment list, venue type, and attendee count to produce risks across up to 8 categories: equipment failure, power outage, network, interpretation, weather, crew, timeline, and security.

step3.title: Review and edit risks
step3.text: Each risk shows a title, description, mitigation plan, and severity level (high, medium, low). On Pro and above, you can edit any field, change severity, or remove risks. On Business, you can add custom risks.

step4.title: Include in PDF
step4.text: On Pro and above, toggle 'Include in PDF' to add the risk assessment to your proposal PDF. This shows clients that you've thought through contingencies — a strong professional signal.

riskAssessment.tip: The AI only generates weather risks for outdoor events and interpretation risks when SI equipment is in the proposal. It's smart about what's relevant.

clientPortal.title: Client Portal
clientPortal.content1: The Client Portal gives your clients a dedicated login where they can view all proposals and invoices you've sent them in one place. No more searching through email for share links — everything is organized and accessible.
clientPortal.content2: Clients self-register from the share page using the same email address you sent proposals to. The portal is available on Pro plans and above. You can manage client access from the Clients page in your dashboard.

step1.title: How clients register
step1.text: When you send a proposal, the share page shows an 'Open Client Portal' link at the bottom. Clients click it to create an account with their email and a password. No invite needed from you.

step2.title: What clients see
step2.text: The portal shows two tabs: Proposals and Invoices. Clients see all non-draft proposals and invoices sent to their email, with status badges, totals, and actions to view or download PDFs.

step3.title: Managing access
step3.text: Go to Clients in the sidebar. Clients with portal accounts show a green 'Portal' badge. Click into a client to see their registration date and a 'Revoke Access' button to remove their access.

step4.title: Security
step4.text: Clients can only see proposals and invoices linked to their email address and your company. They cannot see other clients' data, your internal notes, or draft proposals. All access is enforced at the database level.

clientPortal.tip: The Client Portal makes you look more professional — clients see a branded dashboard instead of scattered email links.

proposalComparison.title: Proposal Comparison
proposalComparison.content1: CueQuote's comparison tool lets clients and event planners compare proposals from multiple vendors side by side. It works entirely via share tokens — no login required.
proposalComparison.content2: Paste share URLs or tokens into the comparison page to load proposals. The tool calculates a Value Score for each vendor based on price (40%), scope coverage (35%), and contract terms (25%).
proposalComparison.step1: Navigate to the Compare page and paste proposal share URLs or tokens into the input field to add vendors
proposalComparison.step2: Review the vendor cards showing total price, savings vs cheapest, and Value Score breakdown
proposalComparison.step3: Scroll down to the line item comparison table — items are cross-matched by name and grouped by category, with cheapest highlighted in green and most expensive in red
proposalComparison.step4: Check the Terms Comparison for deposit, validity, cancellation, and insurance differences, then review the AI Insight summary for a recommended choice
proposalComparison.tip: The comparison URL is shareable — send it to your client so they can see the side-by-side analysis themselves

proposalComments.title: Proposal Comments
proposalComments.content1: Comments allow real-time collaboration between you and your clients directly on proposals. Clients can leave feedback on the shared proposal page, and you can reply from the proposal editor.
proposalComments.content2: Comments can reference specific line items and be flagged as formal revision requests. Your team sees a comment badge count in the editor and the system polls for new comments every 10 seconds.
proposalComments.step1: Clients open the shared proposal link and leave comments — they can optionally select a specific line item to reference
proposalComments.step2: When a client flags a comment as a revision request, it appears with a 'Pending' status badge in your editor
proposalComments.step3: Open the proposal in the editor and click the Comments tab — the red badge shows the count of unread comments
proposalComments.step4: Reply to comments and click 'Mark Resolved' on revision requests once you've addressed the feedback
proposalComments.tip: Comments are updated in real-time — both you and your client see new messages within 10 seconds

inventoryManagement.title: Inventory Management
inventoryManagement.content1: Track your physical AV equipment with serial numbers, asset tags, condition ratings, and real-time availability. Assign units to events and see at a glance what's available for upcoming jobs.
inventoryManagement.content2: Each inventory unit links to a catalog item and can be tracked through its lifecycle: available, assigned to an event, in maintenance, or retired. The mini availability calendar shows your weekly equipment status.
inventoryManagement.step1: Go to Inventory and click 'Add Unit' — select equipment from your catalog, enter the serial number, asset tag, purchase details, and condition rating
inventoryManagement.step2: Use the search bar and category filters to find specific units — the table shows equipment name, serial number, condition, status, and current event assignment
inventoryManagement.step3: Click the three-dot menu on any available unit and select 'Assign to Event' — choose a won proposal and dates auto-fill from the event schedule
inventoryManagement.step4: Check the mini availability calendar on the right sidebar — green means available, amber means all units of that type are assigned for that day
inventoryManagement.step5: Use the quick actions to mark units as 'In Maintenance' when they need servicing, or 'Available' when they're ready to deploy again
inventoryManagement.tip: Keep serial numbers and asset tags consistent — they make it easy to track specific units across events and insurance records

crewScheduling.title: Crew Scheduling
crewScheduling.content1: Manage your crew roster, assign team members to events, and share crew prep sheets with your staff. CueQuote supports both in-house staff and freelancers with different rate structures.
crewScheduling.content2: The crew calendar gives you a weekly overview of who's available and who's assigned. The 'Events Needing Crew' widget shows upcoming events that still need staff, and crew prep sheets can be shared as public links with no pricing information.
crewScheduling.step1: Go to Crew and click 'Add Member' — enter their name, type (Staff or Freelancer), default role, skills, and day rate for freelancers
crewScheduling.step2: Filter your roster by type (Staff/Freelancer) or skills (Sound/Lighting/Video) to find the right person for each event
crewScheduling.step3: Click 'Assign to Event' from a member's menu — select a won proposal and the dates auto-fill from the event schedule. You can override their role for this specific event
crewScheduling.step4: Check the 'Events Needing Crew' widget to see upcoming events and their staffing status — click the + button to quickly assign someone
crewScheduling.step5: Share a Crew Prep Sheet via public link — it shows the event schedule, equipment list, and assigned crew without any pricing information
crewScheduling.tip: Crew prep sheets are designed to be printed or shared on mobile — crew members don't need a CueQuote account to view them

costingMargins.title: Costing & Margins
costingMargins.content1: Track your costs and profit margins at the proposal level. Set cost prices on catalog items, define margin targets, and get real-time alerts when a proposal falls below your target profitability.
costingMargins.content2: Cost data is strictly internal — it's never visible to clients in proposals, PDFs, or the client portal. You control which team roles can see cost information through the visibility settings.
costingMargins.step1: Go to Settings > Costing & Margins and set who can view cost data — choose between Owner & Admin only, or include Sales team members
costingMargins.step2: Set your default margin target percentage and optionally override targets for specific categories like Audio, Video, or Labor
costingMargins.step3: Add cost prices to your catalog items, or enter costs per-line-item directly in the proposal editor
costingMargins.step4: Toggle 'Show Costs' in the proposal editor to see the Margin Summary panel — it shows Revenue, Your Cost, Profit, and Margin % with color-coded health indicators
costingMargins.step5: Review margin alerts above your line items — red alerts flag proposals below target, amber alerts flag items missing cost data
costingMargins.tip: The margin calculation only includes required items (not optional ones). Items without a cost price are excluded from the cost total but their revenue still counts — so add costs to all items for accurate margins

vendorManagement.title: Vendor Management
vendorManagement.content1: Manage your AV vendor relationships in one place. Add vendor companies with contact details, track their status, and maintain notes about past experiences and pricing.
vendorManagement.content2: The Vendors page is available in Planner mode. Use it to build your vendor network, send RFQ requests, and compare responses before selecting a vendor for your event.
vendorManagement.step1: Navigate to Vendors from the sidebar (available in Planner mode) and click 'Add Vendor' to create a new vendor record with company name, contact, email, and phone
vendorManagement.step2: Set the vendor status (active, preferred, new) and add tags for easy filtering — e.g., 'audio specialist', 'nationwide', 'budget-friendly'
vendorManagement.step3: Add relationship notes to track past experiences, pricing patterns, and reliability — these notes are private and never shared with the vendor
vendorManagement.step4: Send RFQ requests directly from the vendor profile and track response status (pending, received, declined)
vendorManagement.tip: Build relationships with at least 3 vendors per category so you always have competitive options for your clients

quoteComparison.title: Quote Comparison
quoteComparison.content1: Compare quotes received from multiple AV vendors side by side. The comparison view shows pricing, scope, payment terms, and an AI-generated value score to help you make informed decisions.
quoteComparison.content2: Quotes are linked to your proposals — when a vendor responds to your RFQ, their quote appears in the Quotes section where you can review, compare, and select the best option.
quoteComparison.step1: Go to Quotes from the sidebar to see all received vendor quotes, organized by status (pending, received, accepted, declined)
quoteComparison.step2: Upload vendor quotes as PDFs or enter line items manually — the system tracks pricing, scope, and terms for each vendor response
quoteComparison.step3: Use the comparison view to see vendors side by side — pricing differences, payment terms, and cancellation policies are highlighted automatically
quoteComparison.step4: Select a vendor and mark their quote as accepted — the system updates your proposal with the confirmed pricing
quoteComparison.tip: Always compare at least 2-3 vendor quotes before selecting. The value score weighs price (40%), scope completeness (35%), and payment terms (25%)

marketRateBudgets.title: Market-Rate Budgets
marketRateBudgets.content1: When using CueQuote in Planner mode, the AI generates production plans with market-rate budget estimates instead of fixed catalog prices. Each line item includes a low-high price range based on current market data.
marketRateBudgets.content2: Market-rate budgets help event planners set realistic client expectations before getting formal vendor quotes. The AI also provides crew recommendations, production timeline, and practical tips.
marketRateBudgets.step1: Create a new proposal in Planner mode — describe your event including type, attendee count, venue, and production requirements
marketRateBudgets.step2: The AI generates a complete production plan with budget ranges (low-high) for each category: Audio, Lighting, Video, and Crew
marketRateBudgets.step3: Review the crew recommendations and production timeline — the AI suggests staffing levels and setup schedules based on event complexity
marketRateBudgets.step4: Use the budget estimate to align with your client, then request formal quotes from vendors to get final pricing
marketRateBudgets.tip: Market-rate estimates are based on industry averages and may vary by region. Always get formal vendor quotes for final budgeting

feedbackSupport.title: Feedback & Support
feedbackSupport.content1: CueQuote has a built-in feedback system that lets you report bugs, request features, or get support — all without leaving the app.
feedbackSupport.content2: Every submission includes automatic context (your browser, plan, and current page) so our team can help faster. You can track the status of your submissions and see replies directly in the app.
feedbackSupport.step1: Go to Feedback & Support in the sidebar and choose your feedback type: Bug Report, Feature Request, General Feedback, or Support Request
feedbackSupport.step2: Fill in the subject and details — the app automatically captures your browser, plan, and page context
feedbackSupport.step3: View your past submissions in the My Submissions tab — each shows a status badge (Submitted, In Review, Planned, Shipped)
feedbackSupport.step4: Check the Help Center tab for links to tutorials, documentation, and answers to common questions
feedbackSupport.tip: Feedback from Pro and Business plan users is automatically prioritized for faster response

catalogSuggestions.title: Growing Your Catalog with AI
catalogSuggestions.content1: When CueQuote's AI generates a proposal, it sometimes includes items that aren't in your equipment catalog — marked with [CUSTOM] and estimated prices.
catalogSuggestions.content2: After generation, an amber suggestion bar appears showing these new items. You can add them to your catalog with one click, so future proposals use your exact pricing instead of estimates.
catalogSuggestions.step1: Generate a proposal with AI — if any items aren't in your catalog, you'll see a suggestion bar on the Review step
catalogSuggestions.step2: Click the bar to expand it and see each new item with its category, unit, and suggested price
catalogSuggestions.step3: Click 'Add to Catalog' on individual items, or 'Add all' to save them all at once — they'll appear in your Catalog immediately
catalogSuggestions.tip: Items added from AI suggestions keep the AI-estimated price as a starting point — review and adjust prices in your Catalog to match your actual rates

plannerBudget.title: Understanding Your Event Budget
plannerBudget.content1: When you generate a budget plan in Planner mode, CueQuote's AI creates a comprehensive event production budget with market-rate pricing, crew recommendations, and a suggested timeline.
plannerBudget.content2: Unlike AV Company mode which uses your catalog prices, Planner mode uses real market rate ranges so you know what to expect when requesting quotes from AV vendors.
plannerBudget.step1: Switch to Planner mode and describe your event — include venue, attendee count, and what you need (presentations, live music, branding, etc.)
plannerBudget.step2: Review the Budget Overview showing your total estimated range (e.g. €12,500 — €18,200) with a breakdown of equipment vs crew costs
plannerBudget.step3: Check the Equipment & Services section — each item shows why it's needed and a budget range, not just a single price
plannerBudget.step4: Review Crew Recommendations to see which technical roles you'll need, how many people, and the typical daily rate range
plannerBudget.step5: Read the Event Timeline for a suggested schedule, and the Pro Tips section for practical advice on working with AV vendors
plannerBudget.tip: Use the budget range when requesting quotes from vendors — if a quote falls outside the range, ask the vendor to explain the difference
